verses.sanskrit: बृहदश्व उवाच। दमयन्ती तु तच्छ्रुत्वा भृशं शोकपरायणा। शङ्कमाना नलं तं वै केशिनीमिदमब्रवीत्॥१॥
verses.english: Brihadashva said : Having heard all these, Damayanti became afflicted with sorrow; and, suspecting that le must be Nala, addressed Keshini, saying,

verses.sanskrit: गच्छ केशिनि भूयस्त्वं परीक्षां कुरु बाहुके। अब्रुवाणा समीपस्था चरितान्यस्य लक्षय॥२॥
verses.english: "O Keshini, do you go again and scrutinize the conduct of Bahuka; and keeping yourself in silence at his side, behold all his bevaviours.

verses.sanskrit: यदा च किञ्चित्कुर्यात्स कारणं तत्र भामिनि। तत्र सञ्चेष्टमानस्य लक्षयन्ती विचेष्टितम्॥३॥
verses.english: O beautiful one, find out the cause, whenever he does anything; and marks well whenever he performs anything skillful.

verses.sanskrit: न चास्य प्रतिबन्धेन देयोऽग्निरपि केशिनि। याचते न जलं देयं सर्वथा त्वरमाणया॥४॥
verses.english: O Keshini, whenever he may ask fire or water, you will not be in a hurry to give it; and thus obstruct him.

verses.sanskrit: एतत्सर्वं समीक्ष्य त्वं चरितं मे निवेदय। निमित्तं यत्त्वया दृष्टं बाहुके दैवमानुषम्॥५॥
verses.english: "Seeing all these, do you let me know his conduct, as also what human or super-human will be seen in Bahuka. Do you also report to me what else you will see in him."

verses.sanskrit: यच्चान्यदपि पश्येथास्तच्चाख्येयं त्वया मम। दमयन्त्यैवमुक्ता सा जगामाथ च केशिनी॥६॥
verses.english: Thus spoken by Damayanti, Keshini went away. Having learnt the behaviours of that person, who was versed in the knowledge of horses, Keshini returned.

verses.sanskrit: निशम्याथ हयज्ञस्य लिङ्गानि पुनरागमत्। सा तत्सर्वं यथावृत्तं दमयन्त्यै न्यवेदयत्। निमित्तं यत्तया दृष्टं बाहुके दिव्यमानुषम्॥७॥
verses.english: She reported to Damayanti the whole history, mentioning what human superhuman she saw in Bahuka.

verses.sanskrit: केशिन्युवाच। दृढं शुच्युपचारोसौ न मया मानुषः क्वचित्। दृष्टपूर्वः श्रुतो वापि दमयन्ति तथाविधः॥८॥
verses.english: Keshini said: O Damayanti, I have never heard or seen before any person of his character, having so great a 'power over the elements.'

verses.sanskrit: ह्रस्वमासाद्य सञ्चारं नासौ विनमते क्वचित्। तं तु दृष्ट्वा यथा सङ्गमुत्सर्पति यथासुखम्॥९॥
verses.english: Whenever he comes to a narrow hole, he never stoops low; rather the hole opens wide at his touch; and he easily passes through it.

verses.sanskrit: सङ्कटेऽप्यस्य सुमहान्विवरो जायतेऽधिकः। ऋतुपर्णस्य चार्थाय भोजनीयमनेकशः॥१०॥
verses.english: Thus a small hole grows largely wide at his coming. There were sent by the king (Bhima) various sorts of food, as also flesh of many animals, for Rituparna. There were also many vessels sent for washing the flesh.
verses.bhavadeepa: संचारं द्वारं ह्रस्वमपि उत्सर्पति दीर्घं भवति ॥९॥

verses.sanskrit: प्रेषितं तत्र राज्ञा तु मांसं बहु च पाशवम्। तस्य प्रक्षालनार्थाय कुम्भास्तत्रोपकल्पिताः॥११॥
ते तेनावेक्षिताः कुम्भाः पूर्णा एवाभवंस्ततः। ततः प्रक्षालनं कृत्वा समधिश्रित्य बाहुकः॥१२॥
verses.english: Those vessels, whenever looked at by him (Bahuka), became at once filled with water. Thereupon Bahuka washed them and set himself to cooking. Then again he grasped a handful of grass and held it to the sun, where suddenly fire blazed up.

verses.sanskrit: तृणमुष्टिं समादाय सवितुस्तं समादधत्। अथ प्रज्वलितस्तत्र सहसा हव्यवाहनः॥१३॥
तदद्भुततमं दृष्ट्वा विस्मिताहमिहागता। अन्यच्च तस्मिन्सुमहदाश्चर्यं लक्षितं मया॥१४॥
verses.english: Beholding that greatest wonder, I was struck with astonishment and have come hither. Also another great wonder was marked by me in him.
verses.bhavadeepa: वह्निजयमाह तृणेति त्रिभिः । सवितुः सकाशात् समादधत् उद्दीपितवान् ॥१३॥

verses.sanskrit: यदग्निमपि संस्पृश्य नैवासौ दह्यते शुभे। छन्देन चोदकं तस्य वहत्यावर्जितं द्रुतम्॥१५॥
verses.english: O beautiful one, although he touched fire, still he was not burnt. The water, falling at his command, flowed rapidly.

verses.sanskrit: अतीव चान्यत्सुमहदाश्चर्यं दृष्टवत्यहम्। यत्स पुष्पाण्युपादाय हस्ताभ्यां ममृदे शनैः॥१६॥
verses.english: I have marked another wonder, which was extraordinarily great, that he took some flowers in his hands and pressed them slowly. Although these flowers were pressed by him with the hands, yet they, instead of losing their original forms, became more fragrant and beautiful than before. Observing those marks of wonder, I have hastily come here.

verses.sanskrit: मृद्यमानानि पाणिभ्यां तेन पुष्पाणि नान्यथा। भूय एव सुगन्धीनि हृषितानि भवन्ति हि। एतान्यद्भुतलिङ्गानि दृष्ट्वाऽहं द्रुतमागता॥१७॥
verses.bhavadeepa: वायुजयमाह अतीवेति द्वाभ्याम् । पुष्पेषु क्षीणोंऽशो झटिति वायुना अपूर्यत इत्यर्थः ॥१६॥

verses.sanskrit: बृहदश्व उवाच। दमयन्ती तु तच्छ्रुत्वा पुण्यश्लोकस्य चेष्टितम्। अमन्यत नलं प्राप्तं कर्मचेष्टाभिसूचितम्॥१८॥
verses.english: Brihadashva said : Having heard of those wonderful behaviours of that righteous one and having known him by his acts, Damayanti considered that Nala was obtained.

verses.sanskrit: सा शङ्कमाना भर्तारं बाहुकं पुनरिङ्गितैः। केशिनीं श्लक्ष्णया वाचा रुदती पुनरब्रवीत्॥१९॥
verses.english: Again, by these marks suspecting Bahuka to be her husband, Damayanti wept and again addressed Keshini in a sweet speech, "O handsome one, do you go again and fetch here from the kitchen, without the knowledge of Bahuka, some meat cooked by him." The beneficent lady instantly went to Bahuka; and immediately returned, taking some hot meat therefrom.

verses.sanskrit: पुनर्गच्छ प्रमत्तस्य बाहुकस्योपसंस्कृतम्। महानसाच्छ्रितं मांसमानयस्वेह भाविनि॥२०॥
verses.bhavadeepa: बाहुकं बाहुकरूपिणामिति रूपभेदात्संशयोऽस्ति न तु क्रियात इत्यर्थः ॥१९॥

verses.sanskrit: सा गत्वा बाहुकस्याग्रे तन्मांसमपकृष्य च। अत्युष्णमेव त्वरिता तत्क्षणात्प्रियकारिणी॥२१॥
दमयन्त्यै ततः प्रादात्केशिनी कुरुनन्दन। सा चितानलसिद्धस्य मांसस्य बहुशः पुरा॥२२॥
verses.english: O descendant of the Kuru race, thereupon Keshini gave the meat to Damayanti, who had, during the past days, very often tasted meat boiled by Nala.

verses.sanskrit: प्राश्य मत्वा नलं सूतं प्राक्रोशद्भृशदुःखिता। वैक्लव्यं परमं गत्वा प्रक्षाल्य च मुखं ततः॥२३॥
verses.english: Thus tasting the meat brought by her female servant, she decided the charioteer to be Nala himself; and, inuch aggrieved, she wept bitterly. Overtaken by great calamity, she then washed her face. O Bharata, thereafter she sent her two children with Keshini. Bahuka recognised Indrasena with her brother. Thereupon the monarch (in the guise of Bahuka) came up speedily and, embracing his children, placed them on his lap. Then again, embracing his children, who were like the children of the celestials, Bahuka became filled with the greatest misery and wept bitterly in a soft voice. Thus having cxprcsscd his mental derangement over and over again, the prince of the Nishadhas left the children all on a sudden and spoke Keshini there words,

verses.sanskrit: मिथुनं प्रेषयामास केशिन्या सह भारत। इन्द्रसेनां सह भ्रात्रा समभिज्ञाय बाहुकः॥२४॥
अभिद्रुत्य ततो राजा परिष्वज्याङ्कमानयत् । बाहुकस्तु समासाद्य सुतौ सुरसुतोपमौ॥२५॥
भृशं दुःखपरीतात्मा सुस्वरं प्ररुरोद ह। नैषधो दर्शयित्वा तु विकारमसकृत्तदा। उत्सृज्य सहसा पुत्रौ केशिनीमिदमब्रवीत्॥२६॥
इदं च सदृशं भद्रे मिथुनं मम पुत्रयोः। अतो दृष्ट्वैव सहसा बाष्पमुत्सृष्टवानहम्॥२७॥
verses.english: "O beauteous one, these twins are like iny own children. Hence seeing them suddenly, I shed tears.

verses.sanskrit: बहुशः सम्पतन्तीं त्वां जनः सङ्केतदोषतः। वयं च देशातिथयो गच्छ भद्रे यथासुखम्॥२८॥
verses.english: If you come to me very often, people may think evil; because we are men of other country. So, O handsome one, do you go away hence with ease."
